text:
incident-bot: Pager — latency SLO breach (p99 streaming) on us-west shared-gpu pool. Affected customers: two high-throughput tenants. Auto-mitigation triggered: fallback to smaller model for some routes. Details: sustained p99 > 1.2s for 3m, streaming stalls observed.

kevin-oncall: saw the alert, joining. Can someone post the top noisy tenants and recent scheduling events?

maria-sre: looking. GPU pool us-west-2/gpu-shared-7. Top issuer: tenant/artemis (~38% of recent kernel io ops), tenant/ursa (~22%). cgroup churn visible: multiple tasks hitting blkio throttle events. p95 only moderately up, tail is where it's bad.

samir-ml: streaming traces show many stalled chunks at token 512-768, waiting on disk read for KV cache misses. Likely high read amplification from a bad workload pattern on artemis.

jen-platform: I see cgroup throttling counters spike on node gpu-node-14. dmesg shows repeated NVMe timeouts around the same time window.

nina-se: customers reported degraded interactive sessions — one customer support ticket opened, two more incoming via webhooks. Marking customer-impact: degraded, not complete outage.

kevin-oncall: current mitigations?

maria-sre: autoscale attempted to add nodes but new containers scheduled onto same noisy rack due to AZ capacity; not enough fresh capacity in us-west-2 single AZ. We throttled artemis network egress earlier which helped briefly but not sustained. We've enabled model-fallback policy on top 5 high-latency routes which dropped p99 from ~1.6s to ~1.0s for those routes.

samir-ml: also enabled prefix cache hot-sharding for a subset of sessions to reduce NVMe reads.

kevin-oncall: ok. Can we isolate tenant/artemis? Options: move to dedicated pool, cgroup limit IO, or evict low-priority jobs. Which is fastest?

maria-sre: fastest is cgroup IO limit on those containers. I'll apply a conservative blkio throttle to art* containers on gpu-node-14 to cap read throughput. If that fails we can cordon+drain the node and evacuate the noisy tenant.

jen-platform: before throttling, let's snapshot current cgroup values and notify customers (we've seen misbehaving jobs crash under very tight limits).

maria-sre: copy of current blkio values: 
``` 
# ls -l /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/| grep art
blkio.throttle.read_bps_device: 0
blkio.throttle.write_bps_device: 0
blkio.throttle.read_iops_device: 0
```
Applying: echo "8:0 200000000" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<art_cgroup>/blkio.throttle.read_bps_device

kevin-oncall: proceed with safe throttle, incrementally. notify @nina-se to contact customer ops with a heads up.

nina-se: pinged support, opened incident ticket INC-8421 and added tenants. Sending status update to affected customers: "we are mitigating noisy neighbor IO on your shard, you may see intermittent slowdowns while we rebalance."

maria-sre: throttle applied to artemis group on gpu-node-14 at 200MB/s read cap. Observing metrics in the next 30s.

(30s later)
maria-sre: tail latency dropping — p99 for pool went from 1.6s -> 0.9s, streaming stalls rate down by ~70%. NVMe queue depth on node fell from 45 -> 12.

samir-ml: KV cache miss rate went down for affected sessions. Model-fallback latency also stable. Good short-term win.

kevin-oncall: great. Next steps?

jen-platform: schedule a node drain for gpu-node-14 in 10m, migrate artemis to a less contended node or to a temporary dedicated pod if available. I'll create a drain doc and a rollout plan.

maria-sre: agreed. I'll keep throttle in place until migration completes and then gradually lift. If migration fails, plan B is to move artemis to dedicated capacity or rollback recent app changes from them if they deployed something hot.

nina-se: logging customer comms: "We applied a temporary IO cap to reduce interference; we will follow up with post-incident summary and recommendations (e.g., sharding, cache warm-up)."

deploy-bot: Scheduled migration job 49231 queued. ETA 8m. Will attempt live volume remap then container restart.

kevin-oncall: handing off to night on-call @maria-sre for post-mitigation monitoring. I'll update the incident channel and mark as "mitigated but monitoring". If p99 creeps back above 1.1s for 5m escalate to SE on-call.

maria-sre: taking over rotation. I'm keeping a watch on streaming stalls dashboard and node-level IO. Will post updates every 15m or on any regression.

samir-ml: follow-up action items: add KV warm-up in our client LRU for large-batch tenants, add alert for sustained blkio throttle events per node, add tenant-level cost/IO quota suggestion in Optimize.

kevin-oncall: nice runbook additions. Nina/ops: please coordinate customer follow-up and any potential credits. Keep incident open until migration completes and 30m stable after lift.

nina-se: confirmed. I'll prepare a short post-incident note and attach timeline + mitigation steps.

maria-sre: migration started. Containers being evicted from gpu-node-14 -> drain proceeding, cpu/capacity checks ok.

(8m later)
maria-sre: migration complete, artemis now running on gpu-node-22 (less contended). Gradually removing throttle on gpu-node-14. Observed stable p99 ~0.85s, no new stalls.

kevin-oncall: closing alert as mitigated, leaving incident open for postmortem. Great coordination — documented throttling commands and migration steps in incident tracker.

nina-se: postmortem owners assigned: maria-sre (writeup), samir-ml (root cause analysis & remediation), jen-platform (runbook + alert tuning), kevin-oncall (customer summary). Due EOD tomorrow.

kevin-oncall: thumbs up :thumbsup: — if anything regresses ping me immediately.

maria-sre: acknowledged, monitoring continues."
